_comment: INV-11's root allowlist, as data. `rootlayout_gate.py` compares the repository root with
this file in both directions: an entry not listed here is red (a new top-level directory
appeared), and a listed entry that no longer exists is red (the list drifted stale, which
would let the first rule pass while nobody notices the inventory is fiction).
Three groups, because they have three different owners:
template  -- shipped by fcpp v0.3.11, verified by scaffold_gate.py; adding one of these is
an upstream change, not a local decision
project   -- this repository's own content (INV-11's allowed set)
toolchain -- agent/tool state that lives in the tree but is not shipped (git-ignored or
tool-owned); listed so its presence is a decision rather than a surprise
The rule exists because the cheapest way to add a tool is a new top-level directory, and the
cheapest way to make a repository unreadable is to do that a dozen times. Tools go under
workspace/ unless they must run in CI, and then the answer is usually 'check the artefact in
